questions.question: Which of the following statements are correct about incomplete dominance? 1. The F1 phenotype is intermediate between the two parental phenotypes 2. F2 phenotypic and genotypic ratios are the same (1 : 2 : 1) 3. Incomplete dominance occurs due to the blending of genes 4. It violates Mendel’s principle of dominance
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, alleles do not blend but rather both influence the phenotype. The genes retain their identity

questions.question: Assertion
options: : In codominance, both alleles express themselves independently in heterozygous condition. Reason (R): This results in an intermediate phenotype like in the case of pink flowers in Mirabilis Jalapa
A and R are true; R is the correct explanation of A
A and R are true; R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, R is false (D) A is false, R is true
questions.explanation: The Reason describes incomplete dominance, not codominance. In codominance, like in ABO blood groups, both alleles are fully expressed.

questions.question: A cross between a red-flowered (RR) and white-flowered (rr) Mirabilis Jalapa plant results in all pink-flowered plants in F1. What will be the phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation?
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, F2 shows a 1 : 2 : 1 phenotypic as well as genotypic ratio.

questions.question: Which of the following features is/are true regarding multiple alleles? 1. More than two alleles exist in a population. 2. An individual can carry all multiple alleles. 3. Example includes coat colour in rabbits. 4. ABO blood groups are due to multiple alleles
questions.explanation: Statement 2 is incorrect—only two alleles can exist in an individual, even if the population has multiple alleles

questions.question: Match the Following Column A Column B A) Sickle Cell Anaemia 1) Affects shape of RBC, causes anemia B) Phenylketonuria 2) Mental retardation, skin pigmentation C) Marfan Syndrome 3) Affects eyes, heart, and skeleton
questions.explanation: These are all examples of pleiotropy, where one gene affects multiple traits.

questions.question: In a dihybrid cross involving seed shape (round/dominant, wrinkled /recessive) and seed color (yellow/dominant, green/recessive), what phenotypic ratio is expected in F2?
questions.explanation: This is a classic Mendelian dihybrid cross, showing independent assortment.

questions.question: In ABO blood grouping, if a child has blood group AB, which of the following parental combinations is not possible?
questions.explanation: O group individual has genotype ii and cannot pass I or I allele required to form AB.

questions.question: In incomplete dominance, the heterozygous genotype expresses a phenotype that is _______ to both homozygous conditions
questions.explanation: Pink flower is intermediate between red and white in Mirabilis jalapa. |

questions.question: Identify the incorrect statement
options: Co-dominance results in expression of both alleles independently.
In pleiotropy, a gene can affect multiple traits.
Incomplete dominance leads to blending of genes
Multiple alleles can be found in a population but not more than two in an individual
questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance, phenotypes blend, not the genes. Alleles remain unaltered.

questions.question: A tall pea plant with axial flowers (TtAa) is test-crossed with a dwarf pea plant with terminal flowers (ttaa). What percentage of offspring are expected to be tall with terminal flowers?
questions.explanation: Explanation: Test cross TtAa × ttaa Gametes: TA, Ta, tA, ta × ta Tall (T–) + terminal (aa): only Ta × ta 25%
